research.headline: Attack policy selection significantly misleads AI monitor evaluations
research.summary: An evaluation of an ex-production OpenAI monitor shows that measured false negative rates are highly sensitive to the method and optimization level used to generate attack policies. These variations indicate that evaluations using basic attack methods can provide false confidence, and interpreting results requires justification of the proxies used.

research.headline: METR updates AI time horizon plot showing exponential capability growth
research.summary: A new report from AI evaluation nonprofit METR indicates that AI capabilities continue to improve exponentially. However, the findings reveal that models struggle more with tasks requiring judgment compared to coding.

research.headline: Researchers Introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer to Balance Expressivity and Efficiency
research.summary: The Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT) uses keys and values as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops to push the expressivity-efficiency frontier of looped Transformers. Variants like U-shaped MoLT balance efficiency and quality by separating memory construction from prediction readout and skipping unused decoder traversals. In pretraining evaluations, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 models and lowers cross-entropy on continued pretraining baselines.

research.headline: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
research.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing.

research.headline: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
research.summary: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together.

titans.headline: Amazon Discusses Potential Lifting of Muse AI Shopping Block
titans.summary: Amazon has held discussions regarding ending its block on Meta's Muse AI agent to allow it to shop on the online marketplace. The talks focus on product recommendations and the potential impact on Amazon's advertising revenue, according to a Fortune report.

titans.headline: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
titans.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket's Marisa Kabas. During the meeting, Huang […].

regulatory.headline: SHEIN Agrees to Pay $100 Million to Settle FTC Deceptive Practice Allegations
regulatory.summary: SHEIN will pay $100 million in consumer redress to settle Federal Trade Commission allegations that the fast-fashion retailer engaged in unfair customer service practices and deceived consumers. The FTC claims SHEIN made purchase resolutions difficult, failed shipping promises, suppressed negative reviews, and made deceptive supply chain and cotton-origin claims.

regulatory.headline: FTC Finalizes Antitrust Order on Beretta and Ruger Stock Agreement
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission has finalized an order addressing antitrust concerns regarding a stock purchase agreement between firearm manufacturers Beretta Holding S.A. and Sturm, Ruger & Co. Inc. The order prohibits anticompetitive entanglements between the two companies.

regulatory.headline: FTC Narrows 2018 Northrop Grumman Order to Large Solid Rocket Motors
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission has partially granted and partially denied a petition from Northrop Grumman Corporation. The agency modified its 2018 order regarding the acquisition of Orbital ATK, narrowing its scope to apply exclusively to missile competitions involving large solid rocket motors.

regulatory.headline: Ten Additional States Join FTC Lawsuit Against Dollar General
regulatory.summary: Ten states have joined the Federal Trade Commission's amended complaint as co-plaintiffs in a lawsuit against Dollar General Corporation. The suit alleges the company engaged in deceptive pricing practices by charging customers more at the register than advertised prices.

macro.headline: Futures point to Black Friday gains on Wall Street as global markets welcome U.S. resilience
macro.summary: A rebound off lows for the S&P 500 on Wednesday calms bourses after the tech washout.

frontier.headline: Neural Network Decoders For Qubit Loss
frontier.summary: Qubit loss is a significant source of error in many quantum hardware platforms, requiring circuits that periodically replace or reset qubits to maintain fault-tolerance. When the reset process includes loss-resolving measurements, this information can improve decoding and substantially reduce overhead compared to the case where this information is not available. Prior work has demonstrated loss-tolerant circuits for the surface code that show significantly improved thresholds and subthreshold scaling by incorporating loss information.

frontier.headline: Schrödinger's Legacy: The Wave Function and Quantum Reality
frontier.summary: The article discusses how Schrödinger arrived at the formulation of wave mechanics and his legacy on the philosophy of quantum mechanics, focusing in particular on the metaphysics of the wave function. Schrödinger's interpretation of the wave function as electron charge density is generally dismissed or presented only as a curious historical example in the literature. On a closer look, however, while this interpretation was eventually abandoned in favor of Born's statistical interpretation, Schrödinger's idea survived in modern realist approaches to the wave function, such as the mass-density approach and the multi-field interpretation.

frontier.headline: Transition Path Sampling for Rare Events in Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems
frontier.summary: Rare transitions govern the dynamics of many open quantum systems, but their probabilities and rates are difficult to calculate. Transition path sampling (TPS) of quantum systems has so far been limited to Markovian, perturbative descriptions. Here, we formulate TPS for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion, which is exact for Gaussian baths, extending it to non-Markovian and strongly coupled open quantum systems.

frontier.headline: Protein redesign boosts DNA insertion activity and reveals how molecular machinery selects targets
frontier.summary: Genome engineering is exciting, given its vast potential to treat and even cure diseases, but it is still a largely uncharted biomedical innovation. Jude Children's Research Hospital recently uncovered the mechanisms involved in precisely integrating DNA into a target genomic location using CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs). By studying type I-F3 CAST, the researchers unveiled structural findings that explain how this CAST family achieves successful DNA integration at precise target sites and offer insights for future genomic engineering approaches.

frontier.headline: Complementary mechanisms of critical quantum metrology
frontier.summary: Critical metrology conventionally exploits enhanced susceptibility to a system parameter near a phase transition. Here we identify a complementary mechanism for critically enhanced estimation of intrinsic system parameters via suppressed quantum noise rather than enhanced response. We demonstrate both mechanisms in coherently radiating spin states (CRSS)-correlated states of $N$ spin-$1/2$ particles defined as asymptotic eigenstates of the collective-spin lowering operator with complex eigenvalue $r e^{-i\varphi}$.

industry.headline: Inside the Chinese City Where Furniture Dupes Are Made
industry.summary: Across social media, influencers share the fake luxury pieces they got directly from China—for one-tenth the price. Here’s where that viral sofa came from.

voices.headline: Conservatives promote Western civilization narrative to justify dominance and power
voices.summary: Donald Trump's administration and the MAGA movement have increasingly framed the United States as the exclusive defender of Western civilization. This ideological project relies on an outdated historiography that views human progress as the product of ethnic homogeneity and isolation rather than cross-cultural exchange. Critics argue this narrative serves to legitimize power and dominance while ignoring the interconnected nature of antiquity.

voices.headline: Donald Trump successfully pushes to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
voices.summary: Donald Trump intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO despite reports linking Huang to a Chinese spy and concerns over advanced chips reaching China. Trump dismissed national security implications, even discussing the matter with Chinese President Xi Jinping. His actions reflect a disregard for national interests and a prioritization of the stock market.

voices.headline: Congressional Democrats divided over passing the bipartisan infrastructure permitting reform bill
voices.summary: Democratic lawmakers in Congress are split over supporting the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which aims to streamline infrastructure and energy projects. While some green-energy champions back the reform to accelerate decarbonization, traditional environmental groups oppose it to maintain existing regulatory hurdles. Consequently, the party's internal division threatens the passage of a bill designed to lower energy costs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

voices.headline: Adapting the Scandinavian Compromise for American Economic Renewal
voices.summary: The author proposes adopting a Scandinavian-inspired economic model that combines robust social welfare and inclusion with aggressive free-market dynamism. By balancing progressive safety nets with conservative free-trade and deregulatory principles, the United States can address declining productivity and pervasive economic insecurity without total partisan victory.

voices.headline: The Great American Tradition
voices.summary: In September, after the White House barred CNN journalists from its grounds, some of the top news organizations in the country suspended their pooled coverage there. The Department of Justice is now investigating them for this act of defiance. In a statement, a department spokesperson accused the networks of having “proudly boycotted covering White House events” and warned that “group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act.” This argument is not a new one.
